source_text: Quae praevaricatio licet non sit facta naturalis, fuit tamen forma peccati atque ob hoc licet non aggravet nascentes, tamen accusat imitantes.
pass_a_gloss: Which transgression, although it was not made natural, was nevertheless a form of sin and on this account, although it does not weigh down those being born, nevertheless accuses those imitating.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nascor; Blaise infants in the original-sin debate

pass_b_english: Although this transgression did not become natural, it was nevertheless a model of sin. Thus, although it does not burden those who are born, it accuses those who imitate it.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Adam's act of crossing the command; Julian's example of sin, not a transmitted nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
